note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe diarrhea for 3 days; began as watery stools, now very loose; at least 4 episodes today, previously more frequent.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms started 3 days ago, ongoing without improvement.
- Associated symptoms: High subjective fever ("literally boiling"), frequent vomiting (unable to keep down fluids or solids), abdominal pain centered around the navel (sore to touch), pain triggers urge to defecate; no blood in stool or urine; no rash.
- Context/triggers: No recent travel; brother and others at his school have similar symptoms; likely infectious contact within household.
- Prior history: No similar previous episodes; normal bowel habits (once daily).
- Urination: Last urinated about 1 hour ago; normal frequency, color not assessed.

Past Medical History:
- No history of chronic medical conditions or previous abdominal issues.
- Experiences occasional menstrual cramps, managed with occasional ibuprofen.
- No previous surgeries.
- Allergies: Not recorded.
- Medications: Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Substance use: Does not smoke; drinks alcohol occasionally ("a pint from time to time"); no recreational drug use.
- Diet: Eats normally when well; currently unable to tolerate oral intake.

Physical Examination:
- Subjectively febrile.
- Abdominal pain: Peri-umbilical, sore to touch.
- No rash.
- Passed urine within the past hour.
- No blood in stool or urine.
- No objective examination findings or vital signs recorded.

Impression:
- Likely acute infectious gastroenteritis (viral etiology favored due to family/household cluster and community outbreak).
- Differential diagnosis: 
    - Viral gastroenteritis (most likely; acute onset, household spread, classic symptoms).
    - Bacterial gastroenteritis (possible; persistent symptoms, requires stool testing for confirmation).
    - Food poisoning (considered less likely due to length of illness and secondary spread).

Management Plan:
- Continue oral rehydration salts (ORS) as tolerated; take frequent small sips (despite current vomiting, attempt minimal intake).
- Advise urgent clinical appointment for assessment of hydration status and stool sample collection to rule out bacterial etiology.
- Dietary advice: Simple foods (e.g., toast, biscuits) only as tolerated; avoid milk, fruit, vegetables.
- Escalation: Seek urgent/emergency care (A&E) if symptoms worsen or unable to pass urine, or if unable to tolerate any fluids.
- Appointment booking via support line.

Patient Summary:
- Patient presents with 3-day history of severe diarrhea, vomiting, and fever, associated with abdominal pain and inability to keep down fluids. Given concurrent illness in household contacts, viral gastroenteritis is most likely. Plan includes urgent clinic evaluation for hydration assessment and stool sample, with supportive care and clear advice about when to seek emergency help.

Key Takeaways:
- Continue to take small, frequent sips of oral rehydration solution.
- Seek urgent medical attention if becoming more unwell, cannot pass urine, or cannot tolerate any fluids.
- Attend clinic promptly for evaluation and stool sample testing.

Next Steps:
- Attend urgent clinic appointment for hydration check and stool testing.
- Monitor for signs of dehydration or worsening condition.
- Follow dietary and hydration advice until reviewed.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: Objective physical exam and vital signs; allergy status not documented; no recent medication reconciliation beyond vitamins/ibuprofen.
● No conflicts between transcript and DDx.
● Transcript: High quality, clear clinical content with minimal noise.
